Arrive in Ecuador’s capital. The transfer from the airport to your hotel takes about 1 hour. Stay at the 4-star Mercure.

**Quito and the equator in 6 hours**

Optional

The tour takes about 6 hours, including transfers.
Honour guards in blue uniforms by wooden doors in Quito, Ecuador

After breakfast at the hotel, transfer to the airport and fly to the Galápagos Islands.

On arrival at Baltra Airport, your guide will meet you, help with your luggage and take you to the bus. It takes about 10 minutes to reach the Itabaca Channel, which separates Baltra from Santa Cruz. Cross by motorboat in about 5 minutes, then drive across the island to Puerto Ayora, about 45 minutes away.

Along the way, you’ll see the landscape of Santa Cruz change from the red, rocky ground of the north to the green highlands. The group will visit the island’s farming area, home to endemic birds, including the finches associated with Darwin’s research.

The focus of the day is the giant Galápagos tortoises in their natural habitat. You can see tortoises of different ages and sizes and learn how privately owned farms help protect their population and habitat.

You’ll also visit the lava tunnels. They formed as lava flows cooled unevenly on their way from the volcano’s slopes to the coast. Some tunnels have collapsed, while the surviving sections let you walk inside and see their structure. The route includes narrow passages and areas with fallen boulders. Your guide will explain how the tunnels formed and why they survived in the Santa Cruz highlands. Allow about 30 minutes for the visit.

Lunch is included. Then transfer to the 4-star Villa Laguna hotel, check in and enjoy some free time in Puerto Ayora. You can walk along the waterfront and browse the souvenir shops.

Meals: breakfast and lunch.
